subject: Coaching T21: 3 MCM color choices -- specific context and reasoning for each
body:
COACHING SUBMISSION T21: Three MCM Color Choices -- The Why
Specific context for each. Not brand guide citations.

---

CHOICE 1: --color-warning: #8A6200 (not the original #E8A317)
Context: Timer warning state in exam.html when under 5 minutes remaining.
The original token (#E8A317) was a bright warm yellow. On white (#FFFFFF) it reads at 2.17:1 -- invisible as a warning label.
I changed it to #8A6200 (5.49:1 on white). Here is the specific reason: this moment IS the highest-stress point in Kai's exam experience. The timer turns amber, the clock is real, ADHD time blindness is fully in play. The warning color is the only signal that says "pay attention to this timer NOW." If that color is invisible against its background, the signal fails when it matters most. #8A6200 is ochre-gold -- it still reads as "amber warning" to Kai's eye while meeting contrast. I did not pick a random passing color. I picked the darkest version of that amber family that still reads as warning, not as brown.

CHOICE 2: #4A90D9 as proposed --accent-blue-on-dark
Context: tier-mid standard card text on dark dashboard background.
--accent-blue (#1D42BA) is Pistons Blue. On #161b22 (dashboard dark card bg) it reads at 2.09:1. I could have used white (#FFFFFF) for maximum contrast. I did not, because:
1. The tier-mid card is a mid-performance state indicator. It should NOT shout as loudly as a Grade 4 result (which uses green). White text on dark would feel like every card is equal urgency.
2. #4A90D9 is the same Pistons blue hue (210 degrees) at higher lightness. It passes at 5.18:1 on dark and reads as "this IS the brand color, adapted for this context" not as "we switched to a different color." Kai sees blue and reads it correctly as the standard she's working toward -- not at maximum contrast, but at enough contrast to be readable while visually subordinate to the correct-green tier.

CHOICE 3: #2ECC71 for --color-correct (arena mode) vs. #1B7D3A (light mode)
Context: correct answer state on exam inputs.
Light mode uses #1B7D3A (dark forest green, 7.78:1 on white). Arena mode uses #2ECC71 (bright emerald, 8.16:1 on #141B2D).
These are NOT the same green. The choice is deliberate:
In light mode, correct green must work against white. A bright #2ECC71 on white reads at 2.54:1 -- unreadable. So light mode uses dark forest green.
In arena mode, I needed a green that reads against very dark backgrounds AND signals success. #2ECC71 is Kai's win color -- it is unmistakably positive in the way dark forest green is not in a dark UI. ADHD reward signaling requires clarity: this color should feel like a win, not like a passed test. The emerald green in arena mode is brighter than correct green in light mode specifically because the dark environment demands more saturation to carry the same emotional weight.
